support.ticket.findSimilar.brief: Find features that already ask for this
support.ticket.findSimilar.description: Search the feature rating for wishes like the one described. ALWAYS call this before opening a feature ticket. If it answers with anything, show the member the closest match and offer to like it instead of filing a duplicate — a split rating is worse than a missing row. Answers with the set of similar features.

support.ticket.create.brief: Open a bug or a feature ticket
support.ticket.create.description: File a ticket from what the member described. Work out the type yourself: `bug` if something is broken, `feature` if something is missing. Write the title the way people say it out loud, and put the full description in `body` — it becomes the first message in the ticket's thread. For a feature, call support.ticket.findSimilar first and only create if nothing fits.

support.ticket.vote.description: Add the member's like to a feature — this is what to do when findSimilar turned up what they were about to ask for. One person, one like; liking twice changes nothing. Needs a ticket in context.

support.ticket.setStatus.description: Set a ticket's status. The 4IR team only — the service refuses anybody else, so do not offer this to a member. `planned` is how the team says it is taking a feature on; there is no priority field. Needs a ticket in context.
